page.layout: One page of running text, with a column of marginal notes in the left margin. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Deo Patre missum venisse in mundum[?] In Christum igitur poena illa corporalis transferri potuit.

Mirabile so-phisma quod unumquisq; nostrum mor-tem aeternam, Divina ju-stitia debeat, & tamen nemo nisi u-nam morte aeterna sub-ire queat.III. Hanc caussam opponunt, nobis non pereuntibus, divina justitia vere peccatis nostris satisfieri nullo pacto potuerit[?].

p.i: Vera n. satisfactio est plena debiti persolutio.
Vnusquisq; autem nostrum mortem aeternam divina iustitia debebat.

Vnusquisque igitur nostrum, nisi nos ipsi facere volebamus, alium habere debuisset, qui pro ipso mortem aeternam subiret: Verum id fieri poterat, cum omnibus hominibus generaliter, si Deus summo iure uti voluisset, aeterna mors eunda[?] esset. Quomodo enim posset quis corporalem poenam, praesertim vero mortem, pro alio solvere, quam ipsemet debeat?
Vnum autem quempiam, qui morti aeternae utpote qui nihil deliquisset, minime obnoxium in ventus[?] fuerit, pro omnibus satisfacere potuisse plane ridiculum est cogitare, nedum asserere.

Nam perinde est, ac si quis diceret, unum, qui nihil ipse debeat, et centum tantummodo aureos nummos habeat, quos dare posset pro innumeribus aliis, qui singuli aureos nummos centum debeant, posse satisfacere, cum vix pro uno tantum vere satisfaciendi habeat facultatem. Nemo enim plus, quam unam mortem aeternam subire potest, etiamque pro alio pendere.

page.notes: Right edge of the scan is cut off by the fold and by the neighbouring page; the final words of several lines are partly lost, so they are not fully readable and are marked where needed. The catchword "tura[?]" at the lower right is uncertain. The first line of the final paragraph is cut off. Printed "Nemo" is split across a line end without a hyphen ("N" / "mo"), so it is written whole. The word "in" before "ventus" is at the edge and uncertain. The italic/roman distinction in the "III." paragraph was judged from the scan and may be inexact. The word "eunda" may be a printing error for "eadem". Printed "potuerit" and "mundum" are uncertain at the edges.
